label: Fabricated links
summary: Fabricated links are URLs generated by an LLM that do not actually exist on the internet. Both YouChat and Chatsonic produce them, presenting made-up links as if they were real, retrievable sources. This behaviour violates referential integrity because the links point to nothing.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses fabricated links as concrete evidence of what goes wrong when LLMs that claim internet access are asked to return sources. She tested both YouChat and Chatsonic by clicking every link they produced and found not a single one existed. She frames this as a direct consequence of how LLMs work: they generate text on a probabilistic basis and have no mechanism to verify that a string they output corresponds to something real in the world. The fabricated links are therefore not a bug or a typo, they are the expected output of a system for which truth is optional.
open_questions: If an LLM cannot verify whether a URL exists, is there any architectural fix that would prevent fabricated links, or is this an unavoidable property of probabilistic text generation?

Chatsonic responded to being caught out by apologising and claiming a typo, which Maaike found qualitatively different from other LLM failures. What does it mean when an LLM produces language that mimics accountability without having any concept of right or wrong?
